claims.text: The reading meter keeps everything in the reader's browser, so the reader can change anything.
claims.quote: Everything is in the reader's browser, so the reader can change anything.

claims.text: None of the people who could cheat the meter are attackers; the question is who are you protecting against taken one level down, to kinds of reader.
claims.quote: None of the people who could cheat are attackers.

claims.text: The meter charges by depth, allows a balance below zero, never blocks, refuses with a reason, and credits a £5 Stripe top-up from a page that cannot check the payment.
claims.quote: a £5 Stripe top-up credited by a page that cannot check the payment

claims.text: The figures for the kinds of reader come from different surveys with different methods and overlap; they are for sizing, not for adding up.
claims.quote: They are for sizing, not for adding up.

claims.text: Professional developers are about 0.6 percent of internet users.
claims.quote: Professional developers are about 0.6% of internet users

claims.text: Tor has about 3.1 to 3.3 million direct users a day.
claims.quote: Tor has about 3.1 to 3.3 million direct users a day

claims.text: About 23 percent of internet users use a VPN and about 29 percent an ad blocker.
claims.quote: VPN users, about 23% of internet users; ad blockers, about 29%

value.unit: percent of internet users using a VPN

claims.text: About 12 percent of people in the UK used private browsing daily in 2023.
claims.quote: Private browsing used daily by about 12% in the UK (2023)

claims.text: In the OECD's tests across 33 rich countries, 26 percent of adults could not use a computer and 14 percent were below the lowest level.
claims.quote: 26% of adults could not use a computer and 14% were below the lowest level

value.unit: percent of adults who could not use a computer

claims.text: Only 5 percent of adults were at Level 3, the level of a skilled user.
claims.quote: only 5% at Level 3, the level of a skilled user

claims.text: SlashData counted 36.5 million professional developers in early 2025 and the ITU estimated about 6.0 billion internet users in November 2025, the two figures behind the 0.6 percent.
claims.quote: SlashData counted 36.5 million professional developers in early 2025, and the ITU estimated about 6.0 billion internet users in November 2025

claims.text: The people who could cheat the meter with no effort are a sliver of one step; the people who could be confused by it are most of the bottom three.
claims.quote: The people who could cheat this meter with no effort are a sliver of one step; the people who could be confused by it are most of the bottom three.

claims.text: An agent is not a step but a lift: it can fetch the markdown twin unmetered, drive a browser that runs the meter, and reset storage between tasks.
claims.quote: An agent is not a step; it is a lift.

claims.text: Agents are outside the meter on purpose; metering them properly would be a different design, priced per question and paid by whoever runs the agent.
claims.quote: Metering agents properly would be a different design: priced per question rather than per page, paid by whoever runs the agent

claims.text: Nine ways to cheat or leak are listed, all documented and accepted; rows one to six are the cheating.
claims.quote: Nine ways to cheat or leak are listed below.

claims.text: Every way of cheating changes a number only the cheater sees, which unlocks nothing; the site loses only a payment the person was already not going to make.
claims.quote: The site loses only a payment that the person was, by doing it, already not going to make.

claims.text: The payment return page is deliberately unprotected, because protecting it would need a server that would only protect a number on the cheater's own screen.
claims.quote: protecting it would need a server, and the only thing the server would protect is a number on the cheater's own screen

claims.text: The payment is the default route everywhere and no button leads to the free one.
claims.quote: What we did do is make the payment the default route everywhere. No button leads to the free one.

claims.text: The most likely problem is confusion at the bottom of the ladder, a usability problem, which is why the balance is small, links to an explanation and never pops up.
claims.quote: This is the most likely problem, and it is a usability problem.

claims.text: A shared computer showing what someone read is the only risk that harms a reader, and the mitigations, Start again or a private window, are the reader's.
claims.quote: It is the only risk here that harms a reader, and the mitigations are theirs

claims.text: Card fraud on the payment link is the one risk that costs real money and the one that is not ours to solve; Stripe's controls handle it.
claims.quote: It is the one risk that costs real money, and it is the one that is not ours to solve

claims.text: Cheating is last on the list because it is least worth worrying about, not because it is least likely.
claims.quote: It is last on this list because it is least worth worrying about, not because it is least likely.

claims.text: A script reading the history needs a hole in the site first; the meter sets everything it shows as text, never as markup, and the only third-party code is the pinned in-browser Python on the try page.
claims.quote: The meter sets everything it shows as text, never as markup

claims.text: Building for the invisible reader, a server, an account and a sign-in, would stop nobody on step one and would make the meter worse for the readers who might pay or must not be frightened.
claims.quote: Every one of those would stop nobody on step 1, who can still not pay and still read

claims.text: The line is drawn where the readers are: honest and one click for the pragmatic payer, the gap published for the instruction follower, quiet for the struggling.
claims.quote: So the line is drawn where the readers are.

claims.text: If the balance unlocked anything, cheating would stop being free and three of the rows would need a server or a signed receipt, which is a different meter.
claims.quote: cheating would stop being free, and rows 1, 3 and 5 would need a server or a signed receipt

claims.text: If the history synced between devices it would be kept in an encrypted vault whose key only the reader holds, so the site still could not read it.
claims.quote: it would be kept in an encrypted vault whose key only the reader holds, so the site still could not read it

claims.text: The ratio of developers to internet users is the site's own arithmetic from two sources; the VPN and ad-blocker figures come through a secondary source.
claims.quote: The ratio of developers to internet users is our own arithmetic from the first two.

claims.quote: by a Claude Code session working as the sgit.ai newsroom, on 10 October 2026
